name: Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher (statewide, NYS HCR)
administrator: NYS Homes and Community Renewal (HCR) with county Local Program Administrators
description: HUD-funded rent voucher that NYS HCR runs across the state through local administrators. The voucher stays with the household if it moves, as long as it remains eligible.
eligibility: Age 18+ (or emancipated minor); income within HUD limits; at least one citizen or eligible noncitizen. Preference for elderly and/or disabled households (HUD definition), families with children and homeless households.
upfront_cost: None (HCR warns it never asks families for payments)
ongoing_cost: Usually 30% of adjusted monthly income; can be up to 40% (HUD)
max_benefit: Difference between the payment standard and the tenant share
how_to_apply: Apply online at section8.hcr.ny.gov (MyHousing Portal) for open lists, or on paper with your county's Local Administrator. Help line 833-791-2748.
notes: HCR's Project-Based Voucher lottery list closed July 24. General list status changes by county; check the portal. Preference details from HCR Section 8 Waiting List FAQ (Apr 2026).

name: NYCHA Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher
administrator: New York City Housing Authority (NYCHA)
description: NYCHA's HUD-funded voucher program for New York City. The waitlist is closed, and since Aug 1, 2025 NYCHA has paused outreach and voucher issuance from the general waitlist.
eligibility: Income at or below $56,700 for 1 person when the voucher is issued. Priority 1: mobility-impaired applicants in inaccessible housing; priority 2: elderly (62+) and people with disabilities.
how_to_apply: Closed to new applicants. People already on the list keep contact details current at selfserve.nycha.info. VASH and Stability Voucher referrals are still processed.
notes: Last open June 3-9, 2024; 200,000 applicants were drawn by lottery for the new list (NYS Senate notice).

name: Mainstream Vouchers (NYC HPD)
administrator: NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD), with the Center for Independence of the Disabled, NY (CIDNY)
description: HUD vouchers for non-elderly adults with disabilities who are homeless, at risk of homelessness, or leaving or at risk of entering an institution.
eligibility: Household member aged 18-61 with a disability (e.g., SSI for disability) who is homeless, at risk of homelessness, institutionalized or at risk of institutionalization.
how_to_apply: Contact CIDNY or ask HPD for a Mainstream Voucher Program Interest Form. CIDNY screens and contacts applicants within 15 business days.
notes: The FAQ is dated Aug 2022. Vouchers are limited, and HPD stops taking applications once they are all issued. Whether vouchers are available in 2026 is not published. HCR's 2026 Administrative Plan also has Mainstream and NED chapters, but their text was not verified.

name: HUD Section 811 Project Rental Assistance (PRA)
administrator: HUD, through a state housing agency partnered with the state Medicaid/human services agency
description: Federal rent subsidy attached to specific apartments in affordable buildings, for extremely low-income adults with disabilities who receive community-based long-term services.
eligibility: Income at or below 30% AMI; at least one adult with a disability who is eligible for Medicaid or state community-based long-term services.
how_to_apply: Referral only: the partnered Medicaid/human services agency identifies and refers tenants. There is no direct application.
notes: NOT VERIFIED for New York: no current NY-specific 811 PRA page was found on hcr.ny.gov, health.ny.gov or opwdd.ny.gov. Treat NY availability as unconfirmed.

name: HUD Fair Housing complaints (FHEO) - reasonable accommodation
administrator: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, Office of Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity
description: Federal complaint process for housing discrimination, including denial of reasonable accommodations or modifications for a disability.
eligibility: Anyone who believes they faced housing discrimination.
how_to_apply: Report online at hud.gov/reporthousingdiscrimination, call 1-800-669-9777, or mail the form to the regional FHEO office.
notes: HUD says time limits apply and to file as soon as possible. The exact deadline is not stated on the page.

name: SSI living-arrangement rules (in-kind support and maintenance)
administrator: Social Security Administration (SSA)
description: How where you live and who pays for shelter changes your SSI. Living in someone else's household without paying your share can cut the federal SSI by one-third.
eligibility: SSI recipients.
max_benefit: 2026 federal SSI $994/month. In-kind shelter support can cut it by up to $351.33/month; the one-third reduction is $331.33.
how_to_apply: Report living arrangement and shelter costs to SSA; appointment at local Social Security office.
notes: Food no longer counts as in-kind support since 9/30/2024. Paying your fair share of household costs avoids the reduction.

name: OPWDD eligibility (including autism)
administrator: NYS Office for People With Developmental Disabilities (OPWDD)
description: Eligibility determination that opens the door to OPWDD services. Autism is a named qualifying condition under Mental Hygiene Law 1.03(22).
eligibility: Developmental disability (autism named) that began before age 22, is expected to continue indefinitely and is a substantial handicap. Adaptive scores usually 2.0+ standard deviations below the mean on a normed measure.
upfront_cost: None from OPWDD (outside evaluations may cost money)
how_to_apply: Contact the regional Front Door. Submit psychological report, adaptive behavior assessment, medical and social evaluations from the last 12 months, and developmental history. Three-step review with Fair Hearing rights.
notes: Autism cases are flagged for possible second-step review because severity varies. Eligibility from childhood may need re-confirming in adulthood (Camphill admissions note).

name: OPWDD Front Door
administrator: OPWDD regional Front Door offices
description: OPWDD's single entry point. Staff confirm eligibility, then help with person-centered planning and choosing services, including where to live.
eligibility: Anyone seeking OPWDD services.
how_to_apply: Call the OPWDD Infoline 866-946-9733 and give your county to be transferred to the local Front Door.
notes: Video modules are in 14 languages plus ASL. No processing timelines are published.

name: OPWDD Individualized Residential Alternatives (IRAs) - supervised and supportive
administrator: OPWDD (state-operated) and voluntary provider agencies
description: OPWDD-certified group homes. Supervised IRAs have 24/7 staff (usually 3-8 people, up to 14); supportive IRAs give periodic support to people who need less than 24-hour supervision.
eligibility: OPWDD-eligible; HCBS waiver and Medicaid for residential habilitation; placement prioritized by need through Certified Residential Opportunities (CRO).
ongoing_cost: Resident's SSI goes to the provider minus a personal allowance. 2026 voluntary-operated: $1,429/month SSI (NYC, Nassau, Rockland, Suffolk, Westchester) or $1,399 (rest of state), keep $219. State-operated: $994 SSI, keep $219.
max_benefit: Medicaid pays residential habilitation; amount not published
how_to_apply: Tell your Care Manager you want a certified residential opportunity; Care Manager submits a referral to OPWDD's CRO process.
notes: Personal allowance figures are from OPWDD's revised 2026 SSI chart. Under the CRO process (ADM 2024-03), priority depends on care needs, available natural supports and risk of harm. No wait times are published.

name: OPWDD Family Care
administrator: OPWDD and provider agencies
description: An adult lives in a certified private family's home. The provider is trained, inspected, and reimbursed for room, board and support.
eligibility: OPWDD-eligible adults who want family living and need daily support.
ongoing_cost: 2026: SSI (with Level 1 State Supplement) is $1,260.48/month in NYC, Nassau, Rockland, Suffolk and Westchester, or $1,222.48 elsewhere. The resident keeps a $191 personal allowance; the rest goes to the provider.
how_to_apply: Through Care Manager / CRO request.
notes: People can also become Family Care providers (opwdd.ny.gov/community-involvement/become-family-care-provider).

name: OPWDD Intermediate Care Facilities (ICF/IID)
administrator: OPWDD and voluntary providers
description: 24/7 residences with bundled nursing, clinical and therapy services for people with higher medical or behavioral needs.
eligibility: OPWDD-eligible with ICF level-of-care need; Medicaid.
how_to_apply: Through Care Manager / CRO request.
notes: OPWDD encourages moves from ICFs to smaller homes through the Open Doors Transition Center.

name: OPWDD Housing Subsidy (formerly Individual Supports and Services, ISS)
administrator: OPWDD, administered through provider agencies / fiscal intermediaries
description: State rent subsidy, like Section 8, for OPWDD-eligible adults living in their own apartment or home, alone or with roommates or a live-in caregiver. It also offers a one-time transition stipend for moving costs.
eligibility: Age 18+; OPWDD-eligible; holds lease or deed; separate unit with own kitchen and bath (no room rentals or boarding); must apply yearly for other benefits (SSI/SSD, Section 8, HEAP); cannot receive another housing subsidy such as Section 8.
upfront_cost: Transition stipend up to $3,000 for move-in items. Security deposit equal to the lower of the tenant's first-month share or the county maximum.
ongoing_cost: At least 30% of net income (after a $200/month personal allowance), minus utilities and insurance
max_benefit: Lower of actual rent or the county/bedroom OPWDD Maximum Payment Standard, minus the tenant contribution. 2026 county standards are not published on the pages reviewed.
how_to_apply: Ask your Care Manager or call the OPWDD Infoline 866-946-9733. The DDRO approves; self-direction participants use an OPWDD-approved provider.
notes: The ADM (2022) says Housing Subsidy is 'formerly ISS'. If the person has Section 8, the subsidy is capped at $50. Provider admin fee is $175/month (NYC, Long Island, Orange, Rockland, Sullivan, Westchester) or $125 elsewhere.

name: OPWDD Integrated Supportive Housing (ISH)
administrator: OPWDD with NYS HCR
description: Affordable apartment buildings with some units set aside for people with I/DD. OPWDD pays a rent subsidy and a provider gives on-site support.
eligibility: OPWDD-eligible adults who qualify for the set-aside unit.
max_benefit: Subsidized rent based on 50% AMI for the county, capped at OPWDD's maximum rent
how_to_apply: Ask your Care Manager or call the OPWDD Infoline. Developers and providers apply through the yearly RFA (2026-27 proposals were due July 17, 2026).
notes: Running since 2012. The 2026-27 round offers up to $15M in capital, with I/DD units capped at 25% of a project.

name: OPWDD Self-Direction
administrator: OPWDD; fiscal intermediaries and support brokers
description: Lets an OPWDD participant choose and budget their own supports and staff, including choices about where they live. Can be paired with the OPWDD Housing Subsidy.
eligibility: OPWDD-eligible and enrolled in the OPWDD HCBS Waiver.
how_to_apply: Attend a Self-Direction information session at the regional DDRO, build a Circle of Support, and work with your Care Manager.
notes: Budget amounts are individual and not published.

name: OPWDD Home and Community Based Services (HCBS) Waiver
administrator: OPWDD / NYS Medicaid (1915(c) waiver)
description: Medicaid waiver that pays for OPWDD community services, including residential habilitation, self-direction and home modifications.
eligibility: Developmental disability, appropriate level of need, Medicaid eligibility; must live at home or in a certified Family Care home, community residence or group home at enrollment.
how_to_apply: Submit the Application for Participation (many languages) through your Care Manager.
notes: No processing times are published. 2026 SSI-related Medicaid resource limit is $33,038 (OPWDD 2026 chart).

name: OPWDD Care Coordination Organizations (CCOs)
administrator: Seven CCOs: Advance Care Alliance, Care Design NY, LifePlan CCO NY, Person Centered Services, Prime Care Coordination, Southern Tier Connect, Tri-County Care
description: Care managers who write the Life Plan and handle referrals for residential placement, the Housing Subsidy and self-direction.
eligibility: OPWDD-eligible people (Health Home Care Management or Basic HCBS Plan Support).
how_to_apply: Choose a CCO through OPWDD's Find a Care Manager page.
notes: Each CCO serves 'various counties'. Cost and Medicaid requirement are not stated on the page.

name: OPWDD Open Doors Transition Center (formerly Money Follows the Person)
administrator: OPWDD
description: Helps people move from Intermediate Care Facilities, developmental centers, hospitals or nursing homes into smaller community homes.
eligibility: People living in an ICF, developmental center, or similar institutional setting.
how_to_apply: Through OPWDD's Open Doors / MFP page or your Care Manager.
notes: Funded by Money Follows the Person (federal).

name: New York State Supplement Program (SSP)
administrator: NYS Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance (OTDA)
description: State cash added to federal SSI. The amount depends on living arrangement, and congregate care settings get a larger supplement.
eligibility: SSI-eligible (65+, blind or disabled) NY residents with limited income and resources.
max_benefit: 2026 SSP: living alone $87; with others $23; household of another $23; Congregate Level 1 $266.48 (NYC/LI/Rockland/Westchester) or $228.48; Level 2 $435 or $405; Level 3 $694
how_to_apply: Applying for SSI at Social Security is also the SSP application. OTDA SSP line 1-855-488-0541.
notes: Totals with SSI: $1,081 (alone), $1,017 (with others), $685.67 (household of another), up to $1,688 at Level 3.

name: Access to Home (incl. Access to Home for Medicaid Members)
administrator: NYS HCR, Office of Community Renewal, through Local Program Administrators
description: Grants for accessibility changes such as ramps, lifts, wider doors, roll-in showers and kitchen adaptations, so people with disabilities can stay home.
eligibility: Household income at or below 80% AMI (disabled veterans up to 120%); documented disability with substantial limitation; owner-occupied or rental primary residence; any age.
max_benefit: Up to $25,000 per unit including project delivery
how_to_apply: Individuals cannot apply to HCR. Apply through a funded local municipality or nonprofit listed at hcr.ny.gov/grants-available-through-local-partners.
notes: 2025 round: $5M Access to Home, $5M Heroes and $1.5M Medicaid. In SFY 2024-25, 203 homes averaged $15,354 each (annual report).

name: RESTORE (Residential Emergency Services to Offer Home Repairs to the Elderly)
administrator: NYS HCR through Local Program Administrators
description: Emergency home-repair grants for older homeowners, such as roofs, heat and broken stairs.
eligibility: Homeowners aged 60+; owner-occupied; income at or below 100% AMI.
how_to_apply: Through a local administrator listed at hcr.ny.gov/grants-available-through-local-partners.
notes: Applies only when a parent or relative aged 60+ owns the home the autistic adult lives in.

name: Mitchell-Lama housing
administrator: NYS HCR (state-supervised developments); NYC HPD supervises city developments
description: Moderate-income rental and co-op buildings with income limits and regulated costs, built under the 1955 Limited Profit Housing Companies Act.
eligibility: Moderate-income households; income limits vary by development.
how_to_apply: Apply to individual development waiting lists (see HCR 'Find Affordable Housing').
notes: 269 state-supervised developments were built and 93 have left the program. Income limits and wait times are not on the page. DRIE can freeze rent in Mitchell-Lama units.

name: NY Connects
administrator: NYS Office for the Aging / local NY Connects offices
description: Free, unbiased information and referral for long-term services and supports, for people with disabilities of any age and older adults.
eligibility: People with disabilities of all ages, older adults, families, caregivers.
how_to_apply: Call 1-800-342-9871 or visit nyconnects.ny.gov.

name: NYS Emergency Rental Assistance Program (ERAP)
administrator: NYS Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance (OTDA)
description: Federal pandemic rent relief. New applications are reviewed only where funding remains.
eligibility: Renters with arrears; federal funds are limited to a few counties. Households at 80-120% AMI can apply for state-funded help.
how_to_apply: nysrenthelp.otda.ny.gov. For immediate help, contact your local DSS, myBenefits, 211, or 311 in NYC.
notes: Essentially inactive. Funding is projected only in Dutchess, parts of Nassau, Oneida, Saratoga and parts of Suffolk, with no guarantee. In NYC, use HRA's One Shot Deal instead (not verified here).

name: NYS Division of Human Rights - housing discrimination
administrator: NYS Division of Human Rights (DHR)
description: State agency enforcing the NYS Human Rights Law, including disability reasonable accommodations and modifications and source-of-income protections.
eligibility: Anyone facing housing discrimination in NY.
how_to_apply: File online at dhr.ny.gov/report or call 844-697-3471. No attorney is needed.
notes: Brochure dated April 2026. The filing deadline is not stated in it.

name: NYCHA Public Housing
administrator: New York City Housing Authority (NYCHA)
description: Federally funded public housing apartments across the five boroughs.
eligibility: Income at or below $95,000 for 1 person (NYCHA eligibility page).
ongoing_cost: Not stated on NYCHA page (federal public housing rule is generally 30% of adjusted income)
how_to_apply: Apply online at ApplyNYCHA or at a Walk-in Center kiosk; help line 718-707-7771. Renew every 24 months to keep your place.
notes: A letter should arrive within 30 days. Wait times by borough are not published on the page. Disability Services 212-306-4652.

name: NYC Housing Connect - disability set-asides
administrator: NYC HPD and NYC Housing Development Corporation (HDC)
description: Lotteries for new affordable apartments, with 5% of units set aside for mobility disabilities and 2% for hearing or vision disabilities.
eligibility: Income-eligible for each lottery. Set-aside units need a medical certification (HPD Medical Form). Voucher holders are exempt from minimum income.
ongoing_cost: Rent set by lottery AMI tier
how_to_apply: Apply at housingconnect.nyc.gov; paper applications from HPD 212-863-7990. Housing Ambassadors can help.
notes: Set-aside units are built to UFAS. HPD disability services: accessibility@hpd.nyc.gov, 212-863-6486.

name: CityFHEPS rental assistance
administrator: NYC Department of Social Services / Human Resources Administration (HRA)
description: City rent voucher for households in or at risk of shelter.
eligibility: Gross income at or below 200% FPL plus a qualifying situation: shelter-eligible, referral from a qualifying program, eviction plus prior shelter stay or APS case, or an at-risk veteran.
ongoing_cost: Household share set by household size and income (shown in Household Share Letter)
max_benefit: 2026 maximum rent for 1 person with utilities included: SRO $1,953, studio $2,604, 1BR $2,734
how_to_apply: Through a Homebase office (call 311) or a shelter caseworker. A shopping letter is valid for 120 days.
notes: FAQ dated 01/23/2026. It also mentions a $1,100 figure that conflicts with these charts; confirm with a caseworker.

name: Disability Rent Increase Exemption (DRIE)
administrator: NYC Department of Finance (Rent Freeze Program)
description: Freezes rent for tenants with disabilities in regulated apartments; the city covers future increases.
eligibility: Age 18+; receives SSI, SSDI, VA disability, or disability Medicaid after SSI/SSDI; household income at or below $50,000; rent above one-third of income; rent-regulated, Mitchell-Lama, HDFC or similar unit; named on lease.
how_to_apply: Apply through nyc.gov/rentfreeze (first-time applicants page) or call 311.
notes: Disability-related extension requests are available.

name: NYC Mayor's Office for People with Disabilities (MOPD) - housing resources
administrator: NYC Mayor's Office for People with Disabilities
description: City hub listing accessible housing options, home modification funds, DRIE, Housing Connect set-asides and fair housing contacts.
eligibility: NYC residents with disabilities.
how_to_apply: See the MOPD housing page; NYC Commission on Human Rights 212-306-7450.
notes: Lists Rebuilding Together NYC (718-488-8840) and the Adele Friedman Housing Accessibility Fund for home modifications.

name: Rochester Housing Authority
administrator: Rochester Housing Authority (RHA)
description: Public housing and Housing Choice Voucher programs for the City of Rochester and Monroe County.
eligibility: HUD income limits. 2026 Rochester MSA, 1 person: 30% $22,500; 50% $37,450; 80% $59,950.
how_to_apply: Apply at rochesterhousing.org/apply; lobby at 675 West Main St., Rochester 14611.
notes: Public housing 1-bedroom waitlist closes Oct 26, 2026 at noon, when the studio list opens. Section 8 list status is not stated.

name: Buffalo Municipal Housing Authority (BMHA)
administrator: Buffalo Municipal Housing Authority
description: Federally funded public housing developments in the City of Buffalo.
eligibility: HUD income limits.
how_to_apply: Contact BMHA via bmhahousing.com.
notes: PARTIALLY VERIFIED: the website is active, but its application, waitlist and contact pages could not be read (robots-blocked). Waitlist status is not verified.

name: Syracuse Housing Authority
administrator: Syracuse Housing Authority (SHA)
description: Public housing and Section 8 vouchers in Syracuse.
eligibility: HUD income limits.
how_to_apply: Apply online (waitlistcheck.com/NY752 via syracusehousing.org). 516 Burt St., Syracuse 13202; (315) 475-6181; Section 8 (315) 470-4400.
notes: SHA FAQ: public housing wait usually 6 months-2 years; Section 8 usually 2-5 years.

name: Albany Housing Authority
administrator: Albany Housing Authority (AHA)
description: Public housing in the City of Albany and a Section 8 program.
eligibility: HUD income limits. Preference for working families, or people unable to work because of age or disability, who live or work in Albany.
how_to_apply: Online pre-application at nyalbany.tenmast.com/apply; 200 South Pearl St., Albany 12202; PHEligibility@albanyhousing.org.
notes: Section 8 is closed (a public notice will come before reopening). Public housing 1-5BR applications have been accepted since Aug 31, 2026. All contact is by mail.

name: Municipal Housing Authority for the City of Yonkers (MHACY)
administrator: MHACY
description: Public housing and Section 8 for Yonkers.
eligibility: HUD income limits.
how_to_apply: See 'MHACY's Housing Application Process' at mhacy.org; 1511 Central Park Ave., Yonkers 10710; 914-793-8400; publichousing@mhacy.org.
notes: Section 8 waitlist is closed and is not expected to reopen 'for some time'.

name: The Center for Discovery
administrator: The Center for Discovery (Northwell Health affiliate)
description: Multi-campus Sullivan County nonprofit serving people with complex conditions, including autism. Adult options range from 24-hour nursing homes to five-bed homes on Thanksgiving Farm and community homes.
eligibility: Adults with significant developmental disabilities/autism; OPWDD eligibility expected for adult residential.
how_to_apply: Contact (845) 794-1400 or info@tcfd.org; P.O. Box 840, Harris, NY 12742.
notes: Residential opportunities for 182 adults (2025 overview). Designated a Center of Excellence by NYS DOH and OPWDD. No private-pay cost published.

name: AHRC New York City - Residential Services
administrator: AHRC NYC
description: IRAs, supervised apartments (Opportunities for Independent Living) and 24/7-nursing residences for adults 18+ across all five boroughs.
eligibility: Age 18+; OPWDD waiver-eligible; on OPWDD's CRO list.
ongoing_cost: OPWDD-funded (Medicaid); resident contributes SSI minus personal allowance
how_to_apply: Front Door, then a CCO Care Coordinator submits a CRO request, then AHRC intake. Call 212-780-4491.
notes: Houses 'hundreds of people'. No private fees published.

name: YAI - Residential Services
administrator: YAI
description: Houses and supportive apartments with varied support levels for adults with I/DD.
eligibility: People with I/DD (OPWDD-eligible for NY homes).
how_to_apply: Submit the Getting Started form at yai.org/getting-started; HQ 220 E 42nd St, NYC; 212-273-6100.
notes: Serves NYC, Long Island, Westchester and Rockland (plus NJ and CA). Number of homes and costs not published.

name: The Arc New York (chapter network)
administrator: The Arc New York and its 32 local chapters
description: Statewide network of local chapters; many run group homes, supportive apartments and family supports in their counties.
eligibility: People with I/DD; residential services through OPWDD.
how_to_apply: Find your county chapter at thearcny.org/find-a-chapter; state office (518) 439-8311, Latham.
notes: Chapter-level residential details were not verified individually.

name: Job Path NYC - Supported Living and Self-Direction
administrator: Job Path
description: Helps people set up their own home instead of a group home, with anywhere from a few hours a week to 24/7 support. Its self-direction team helps stretch budgets, including toward rent.
eligibility: OPWDD-eligible adults (see Job Path eligibility page).
how_to_apply: 212-944-0564; info@jobpathnyc.org; 256 W 38th St, 2nd Fl, New York 10018.
notes: Often paired with the OPWDD Housing Subsidy. Costs not published.

name: Life's WORC
administrator: Life's WORC
description: Nonprofit running group homes and a Family Center for Autism for children and adults with I/DD and autism.
eligibility: People with I/DD/autism; OPWDD eligibility for residential.
how_to_apply: Contact via lifesworc.org (Garden City headquarters).
notes: Opened its 45th group home in 2021; serves Nassau, Suffolk, Queens and Manhattan. Homepage confirms it is active. Costs not published.

name: QSAC - Residential Services
administrator: QSAC
description: Autism-focused nonprofit running Individualized Residential Alternatives and Intermediate Care Facilities.
eligibility: Autistic adults, OPWDD-eligible.
how_to_apply: Apply for Services form at qsac.my.salesforce-sites.com/apply.
notes: Serves NYC and Long Island. Costs not published.

name: Anderson Center for Autism - Adult Services
administrator: Anderson Center for Autism
description: Group homes for autistic adults in residential neighborhoods across the Hudson Valley.
eligibility: Autistic adults; OPWDD eligibility expected.
how_to_apply: Call (845) 889-4034; 4885 Route 9, Staatsburg, NY 12580.
notes: Number of homes and costs not published.

name: Aspire of WNY - Residential Opportunities
administrator: Aspire of Western New York
description: OPWDD-certified IRAs, from apartments to small and large homes, with staff available up to 24/7.
eligibility: OPWDD-eligible adults.
how_to_apply: Central Intake (716) 838-0047; intake@aspirewny.org.
notes: 43 group homes supporting 320 people in Erie and Chautauqua counties.

name: Camphill Village Copake
administrator: Camphill Village USA
description: Intentional community where adults with developmental differences live and work alongside others.
eligibility: Age 23+; OPWDD eligibility confirmed; cannot serve people needing 1:1 support.
upfront_cost: $7,500 fee at the start of the 4-week trial visit (OPWDD cannot be billed before residency); no admission fee
ongoing_cost: Billed to OPWDD once a resident; families are asked for donations
how_to_apply: Tour, application, interview, then a 4-week trial visit. 518-329-4851; 84 Camp Hill Rd, Copake 12516.
notes: Large waiting list as of 2023. Warning: the homepage contained injected casino spam text in October 2026, so the site may be compromised. The admissions page content looked normal.

name: Triform Camphill Community
administrator: Triform Camphill Community
description: 420-acre farm and craft community for young adults with developmental disabilities moving into adulthood; residential or day students in 10 homes.
eligibility: Young adults with developmental disabilities.
how_to_apply: See the Enroll section at triform.org; 518-851-9320; 20 Triform Rd, Hudson 12534.
notes: Tuition and funding source not published. federally_funded set to false because no OPWDD/Medicaid funding is stated. The site shows no 2026 dates, so operating status is assumed from a live site.

name: Center for Independence of the Disabled, NY (CIDNY) - Housing
administrator: CIDNY (independent living center)
description: Housing search help, subsidy navigation and eviction prevention for people with disabilities. Not a housing provider. CIDNY is HPD's Mainstream Voucher partner.
eligibility: People with disabilities in NYC.
how_to_apply: 212-674-2300; housing@cidny.org.
notes: Also lists Access to Home, Olmstead Housing Subsidy and Rapid Transition Housing Program.

name: Ticket to Work
administrator: Social Security Administration
description: Free, voluntary SSA program that connects disability beneficiaries with Employment Networks or the state VR agency (ACCES-VR) for job services. It also protects people from medical continuing disability reviews while they are using their Ticket and making progress.
eligibility: Ages 18-64 receiving SSDI and/or SSI based on disability.
how_to_apply: Call the Ticket to Work Help Line 1-866-968-7842 (TTY 1-866-833-2967), M-F 8am-8pm ET, or use the Find Help tool at choosework.ssa.gov.
notes: In NY, ENs include NYS DOL Disability Resource Coordinators' network and many nonprofits; ACCES-VR is the state VR option.

name: SSI/SSDI work incentives (SGA, Trial Work Period, Student Earned Income Exclusion)
administrator: Social Security Administration
description: Rules that let SSI and SSDI recipients work and keep some or all of their benefits. 2026 figures: SGA $1,690/month (non-blind), $2,830 (blind); a Trial Work Period month is any month earning over $1,210; the SSI Student Earned Income Exclusion shields $2,410/month up to $9,730/year.
eligibility: SSDI and/or SSI recipients; SEIE requires SSI recipient under age 22 who regularly attends school.
how_to_apply: Report earnings to SSA; get free benefits counseling from a WIPA provider or NYESS benefits advisor before starting work.
notes: 2026 SSI federal benefit rate $994 individual / $1,491 couple. Also includes Impairment-Related Work Expenses (IRWE).

name: PASS (Plan to Achieve Self-Support)
administrator: Social Security Administration
description: An SSI work incentive that lets a person set aside income or resources toward a specific work goal (training, equipment, a business) without reducing SSI. Money set aside under an approved plan is not counted.
eligibility: SSI recipients or people who could qualify for SSI if not for income/resources set aside; must have a feasible work goal.
how_to_apply: Submit Form SSA-545 to SSA, ideally with help from a benefits counselor (WIPA) or ACCES-VR counselor.
notes: SSA's PASS spotlight page could not be fetched; described from the Red Book table of contents and standard SSA program rules.

name: Section 1619(b) Medicaid while working (New York threshold)
administrator: Social Security Administration / NY State Department of Health
description: Lets SSI recipients keep Medicaid after earnings end their SSI cash payment, as long as earnings stay under the state threshold. New York's 2026 threshold is $68,654 in gross annual earnings.
eligibility: Received at least one month of SSI; still disabled; need Medicaid to keep working; earnings under $68,654 (NY, 2026); resources under $2,000.
max_benefit: Medicaid coverage up to $68,654/yr earnings (2026, NY)
how_to_apply: Automatic through SSA when SSI stops due to work; contact SSA or a benefits counselor to confirm 1619(b) status.
notes: NY 2025 threshold was $64,017. NYESS also lists $68,654 for 2026.

name: Work Opportunity Tax Credit (WOTC)
administrator: U.S. Department of Labor / IRS; certified in NY by NYS Department of Labor
description: Federal employer tax credit for hiring people from target groups, including vocational rehabilitation referrals and SSI recipients. Authorization lapsed December 31, 2025, and the program is in hiatus pending Congress.
eligibility: Employers hiring members of target groups; employees with start dates on/after 1/1/2026 currently cannot be certified.
max_benefit: 40% of first $6,000 first-year wages ($2,400) when authorized
how_to_apply: Employers submit IRS Form 8850 and ETA 9061 to NYS DOL within 28 days of hire; NYS DOL is accepting 2026 applications but may not certify them until ETA authorizes.
notes: LAPSED as of Oct 2026 per NYS DOL page. Also affects NY's WETC, which requires WOTC VR-referral certification.

name: AbilityOne Program
administrator: U.S. AbilityOne Commission (central nonprofits SourceAmerica and National Industries for the Blind)
description: Federal procurement program in which about 400 nonprofit agencies employ people who are blind or have significant disabilities to provide products and services to the federal government. Reports about 41,000 people employed.
eligibility: People who are blind or have significant disabilities, through participating nonprofit agencies.
how_to_apply: Use the 'Find a Job' section of abilityone.gov or contact a participating nonprofit agency.
notes: NYSID is NY's STATE Preferred Source central nonprofit, not an AbilityOne central nonprofit; see separate NYSID entry. No NY-specific AbilityOne site list verified.

name: Job Accommodation Network (JAN)
administrator: U.S. DOL Office of Disability Employment Policy (grant)
description: Free, confidential expert guidance for workers and employers on workplace accommodations and ADA employment questions. Includes an A-Z disability and accommodation database.
eligibility: Anyone: job seekers, employees, employers, families, service providers.
how_to_apply: Call (800) 526-7234 or use the Ask JAN form/live chat at askjan.org.
notes: Active in Oct 2026 (webcasts scheduled Oct 22 and Oct 29, 2026).

name: Schedule A hiring authority (federal jobs)
administrator: U.S. Office of Personnel Management / federal agencies
description: Non-competitive hiring path into federal jobs for people with severe physical, psychiatric, or intellectual disabilities. After two years of satisfactory service, appointees may convert to permanent status.
eligibility: People with intellectual, severe physical, or psychiatric disabilities (5 CFR 213.3102(u)) who meet job qualifications.
how_to_apply: Get proof of disability from a licensed medical professional, licensed VR specialist (e.g., ACCES-VR), or benefits agency; follow Schedule A instructions in USAJOBS announcements.
notes: Proof of disability letter required before hire.

name: ACCES-VR (Adult Career and Continuing Education Services - Vocational Rehabilitation)
administrator: NYS Education Department
description: New York's state vocational rehabilitation agency, offering counseling, assessment, training, job placement, and supported employment funding for people with disabilities. Services are planned with a Vocational Rehabilitation Counselor.
eligibility: Age 14+; disability that affects getting, keeping, or advancing in a job; available to take part in VR. SSI/SSDI recipients are presumed eligible.
how_to_apply: Submit Application VR-04 online, by email to accesvrapplications@nysed.gov (subject 'ACCES-VR Application'), or by mail to a District Office; or call 1-800-222-JOBS (5627).
notes: Order of selection: official pages reviewed (Oct 2026) describe an Order of Selection policy (2003) but do not state that one is in effect; no closed categories found. Unverified - confirm with district office.

name: Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS)
administrator: NYS Education Department - ACCES-VR
description: Five services for students with disabilities: job exploration counseling, work-based learning, counseling on postsecondary options, workplace readiness training, and self-advocacy instruction. Students can receive them before being found eligible for VR.
eligibility: Students with disabilities ages 14-22 (potentially eligible or eligible for ACCES-VR).
how_to_apply: Ask the school, transition coordinator, or local ACCES-VR district office for a Pre-ETS referral.

name: OPWDD Pathway to Employment
administrator: NYS Office for People With Developmental Disabilities (HCBS Waiver)
description: A year-long, usually part-time program to build a job goal and career plan, with job-readiness instruction toward a job at or above minimum wage. Often used by people leaving high school or day habilitation.
eligibility: OPWDD-eligible, enrolled in the HCBS Waiver, with a Care Manager.
how_to_apply: Contact your Care Manager.
notes: Duration: about one year.

name: OPWDD Employment Training Program (ETP)
administrator: NYS Office for People With Developmental Disabilities (HCBS Waiver)
description: A paid internship at a community business, with wages paid through the program while the person learns the job, plus discovery, job development and coaching. The business may then hire the person directly.
eligibility: OPWDD-eligible, HCBS Waiver enrolled, with a Care Manager.
max_benefit: Paid internship wages (at least minimum wage per AHRC NYC)
how_to_apply: Contact your Care Manager.
notes: Supported Employment continues supports after hire.

name: OPWDD Supported Employment (SEMP)
administrator: NYS Office for People With Developmental Disabilities (HCBS Waiver)
description: Ongoing job coaching and supports to keep a paid, competitive community job, including self-employment. People often move here after ETP or ACCES-VR services.
eligibility: OPWDD-eligible, HCBS Waiver enrolled.
how_to_apply: Discuss employment goals with your Care Manager.
notes: Acronym SEMP is not used on the OPWDD page; it is the common name for this service.

name: OPWDD Community Based Prevocational Services
administrator: NYS Office for People With Developmental Disabilities (HCBS Waiver)
description: Part- or full-time services that build workplace skills for people who want to work but need extra help, and can support people already working.
eligibility: OPWDD-eligible, HCBS Waiver enrolled.
how_to_apply: Contact your Care Manager.

name: NYS Career Centers and Disability Resource Coordinators (NY SCION)
administrator: NYS Department of Labor (local workforce areas)
description: Career Centers offer career counseling, resume help, workshops, job search help and possible short-term training. Disability Resource Coordinators provide benefits advisement and work-incentive counseling for SSA beneficiaries and train employers on ADA and accommodations.
eligibility: Any job seeker; DRC benefits counseling for SSDI/SSI recipients.
how_to_apply: Find a center at dol.ny.gov/career-centers; find your county DRC in the DRC table (many counties listed VACANT - contact nearest Career Center or Independent Living Center).
notes: DRC program expanded statewide with $11.1M federal workforce funding (2021).

name: Workers with Disabilities Employment Tax Credit (WETC)
administrator: NYS Department of Labor / NYS Department of Taxation and Finance
description: New York employer tax credit worth 35% of the first $6,000 of wages in an eligible employee's second year of employment, up to $2,100 per employee. Combined with federal WOTC, total possible is $4,500.
eligibility: Employers of employees certified by ACCES-VR or NYS Commission for the Blind who meet WOTC vocational-rehabilitation-referral criteria and work at least 2 years.
how_to_apply: Employers use the WETC Pre-Screening Eligibility Form; questions 518-457-6823.
notes: Depends on WOTC certification, which lapsed 12/31/2025; status for 2026 hires uncertain. tax.ny.gov page could not be fetched.

name: NYS Preferred Source Program - NYSID (New York State Industries for the Disabled)
administrator: NYSID (nonprofit designated under NY State Finance Law preferred source program)
description: NYSID markets products and services made by New York nonprofits that employ people with disabilities to state and local government buyers through no-bid preferred-source purchasing. It funds jobs at member agencies across the state.
eligibility: People with disabilities employed through NYSID member nonprofit agencies.
how_to_apply: See 'NYSID Employment Opportunities' on nysid.org or call 1-800-221-5994.
notes: Number of member agencies not shown on pages reviewed.

name: NYS 55-b / 55-c Governor's Program to Hire Individuals and Veterans with Disabilities
administrator: NYS Department of Civil Service
description: Lets qualified people with disabilities be appointed to entry-level state jobs without a competitive written exam. Up to 1,700 positions under 55-b and 500 under 55-c (veterans).
eligibility: Physical or mental disability; otherwise qualified for the duties. 55-c for veterans with disabilities.
how_to_apply: Submit the 55-b/c application packet with resume (55BC@cs.ny.gov, 518-473-8961 / 866-297-4356); then register on the Recruitment Resources Program Portal (NY.gov ID).

name: Medicaid Buy-In for Working People with Disabilities (MBI-WPD)
administrator: NYS Department of Health / local Departments of Social Services
description: Lets working New Yorkers with disabilities keep or get Medicaid with much higher income and savings limits. Premiums are under a moratorium, so none are charged.
eligibility: Ages 16-64, NY resident, SSA-defined disability, in paid work. 2026 limits per NYESS: earnings up to $80,820/yr, resources up to $33,038 (retirement accounts disregarded).
how_to_apply: Apply at your Local Department of Social Services (NYC: HRA).
notes: health.ny.gov page lists older undated limits ($75,385 income / $31,175 resources); 2026 figures from NYESS.

name: NYESS (New York Employment Services System) benefits advisement
administrator: NYS Office of Mental Health and NYS Department of Labor
description: A single statewide entry point for employment services for people with disabilities, with a locator for credentialed benefits advisors who explain work incentives.
eligibility: People with disabilities in NY.
how_to_apply: Use the Benefits Advisor locator on nyess.ny.gov or call 518-474-7773.
notes: Funding source not stated.

name: NYC: ATWORK
administrator: NYC Mayor's Office for People with Disabilities (MOPD)
description: Self-guided job program that connects New Yorkers with disabilities to jobs and internships with partner employers, workshops, and a Relationship Manager. Accommodations such as ASL, CART and Braille are available.
eligibility: NYC resident, 18+, documented disability; has career goals, resume, and can job search independently.
how_to_apply: Complete the Jobseeker Referral Form to join the waitlist; questions 212-788-7559 or nycatwork@mopd.nyc.gov.
notes: Waitlist. NYC Comptroller review (reported July 2026): 1,268 served and 99 placed in FY2024-25. Citywide; county set to New York (MOPD office).

name: NYC 55-a Program
administrator: NYC Department of Citywide Administrative Services (DCAS)
description: Lets qualified people with certified disabilities be hired into competitive-class City jobs without taking the civil service exam. Candidates must first receive a job offer.
eligibility: Disability certified by ACCES-VR or NYS Commission for the Blind; meets job's education/experience requirements.
how_to_apply: Apply to competitive-class jobs at nyc.gov/jobs and request 55-a consideration on resume/cover letter; 212-386-1701.
notes: No central database of 55-a applicants.

name: NYC Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP) - youth with disabilities
administrator: NYC Department of Youth & Community Development (DYCD)
description: Six-week paid summer jobs and projects for NYC youth, with tailored experiences for youth with disabilities. About 100,000 participants in 2026.
eligibility: NYC residents ages 14-24; proof of disability if applying with a disability.
max_benefit: Ages 14-15 stipend; ages 16-24 paid minimum wage
how_to_apply: Apply online at application.nycsyep.com (2026 deadline Feb 27, 2026); help: DYCD Community Connect 800-246-4646.
notes: 2026 program began July 6, 2026. No separate disability slot count published.

name: Erie County Office for People with Disabilities
administrator: Erie County
description: County office in downtown Buffalo that advocates for residents with disabilities and offers employment information and referral.
eligibility: Erie County residents with disabilities.
how_to_apply: Call (716) 858-6215; 95 Franklin St, Room 651, Buffalo, NY 14202.
notes: County (not city) office; listed as the Buffalo-area local disability office. No Rochester/Syracuse city disability employment office verified.

name: Spectrum Designs - Port Washington
administrator: Spectrum Designs Foundation
description: Custom apparel and promotional products company whose mission is creating jobs for people with autism and other disabilities. Offers tiered onboarding, mentoring, trained managers and an on-site social worker.
eligibility: Adults with autism/neurodivergent job seekers (open positions vary).
how_to_apply: See spectrumdesigns.org/careers or call 516.767.7187.
notes: Percentage of autistic employees not published. Also has NJ and FL sites.

name: Spectrum Designs - Westchester (Pleasantville)
administrator: Spectrum Designs Foundation
description: Westchester location of the autism-focused apparel and promotional products social enterprise.
eligibility: Adults with autism/neurodivergent job seekers.
how_to_apply: See spectrumdesigns.org/careers or call 914.984.9901.

name: Café Joyeux New York
administrator: Café Joyeux / Joyeux Foundation US
description: Inclusive coffee shop at 599 Lexington Ave (E 52nd St) whose crew is about 75% people with intellectual and developmental disabilities, including autism and Down syndrome. Provides training and paid jobs.
eligibility: Adults with IDD (hiring via Café Joyeux).
how_to_apply: See the Team/jobs section at us.cafejoyeux.com or visit the café (M-F 7am-4:30pm, Sat 8am-4pm).
notes: Opened 2023; no closure notice found Oct 2026.

name: South Fork Bakery (and Launch training program)
administrator: South Fork Bakery
description: Nonprofit bakery providing paid employment to adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Its Launch program trains and places adults with disabilities at Suffolk County partner businesses.
eligibility: Adults with disabilities (criteria not published).
how_to_apply: Email info@southforkbakery.org.
notes: Open status inferred from active site (2026 event page); no closure news found.

name: Special Touch Bakery
administrator: Special Touch Bakery
description: Rochester bakery creating employment for people of all abilities; reported in 2022 to employ about 30 people with intellectual and developmental disabilities.
eligibility: Adults with disabilities.
how_to_apply: See specialtouchbakery.org careers page; (585) 359-2253, info@specialtouchbakery.org; 208 Mushroom Blvd.
notes: IDD employment figure from Spectrum News (2022); official page says 'individuals of all abilities'. 2026 site active.

name: Ultranauts
administrator: Ultranauts Inc.
description: Software quality and AI services firm founded 2013 that builds 'cognitively diverse' teams; press describes its team as about 75% autistic. Lists a New York office at 2578 Broadway.
eligibility: Neurodivergent and autistic technologists (job openings vary).
how_to_apply: See the Jobs link on ultranauts.co.
notes: Formerly Ultra Testing; NOT closed - site updated Sept 2026. Work largely remote; share of autistic staff from press, not official page.

name: On Your Mark - Employment Services and Business Initiatives
administrator: On Your Mark
description: Staten Island nonprofit offering job-skills training, placement, coaching, Pathway to Employment, ETP and Supported Employment for people with IDD. Runs businesses including the On Your Mark Chocolatier (639 Forest Ave) and a café.
eligibility: People with intellectual and/or developmental disabilities (OPWDD services).
how_to_apply: Call (718) 720-9233 ext. 5205 (Beth Benjamin, Director of Employment Services); 485 Victory Blvd.
notes: Whether participants staff the businesses not stated.

name: YAI Employment Services
administrator: YAI
description: Supported employment with job coaching and long-term follow-up, plus pre-vocational services and employer training, for people with IDD.
eligibility: OPWDD eligible; ACCES-VR approval for supported employment; live in the Bronx, Brooklyn, Manhattan, Queens, Long Island or Hudson Valley.
how_to_apply: Already OPWDD eligible: submit the Getting Started form (yai.tfaforms.net/f/gettingstarted).
notes: Multi-borough; county set to New York.

name: AHRC NYC Employment Services (ETP, Project SEARCH)
administrator: AHRC New York City
description: Employment Training Program internships across NYC paying minimum wage with job coaching and help moving into a permanent job, plus Project SEARCH internships.
eligibility: People with developmental disabilities over 18 (some youth without disabilities for internships).
how_to_apply: Call Request Services 212-780-4491 (TTY 711); 83 Maiden Lane.
notes: AHRC NYC businesses listed: Superior Direct Care Inc., Hudson River Services (no details on who they employ).

name: AHRC Nassau Employment Services and Business Services
administrator: AHRC Nassau
description: Pre-vocational training, Employment Training Program and Supported Employment for people with IDD, plus agency-run businesses (Wheatley Farms Catering and Commercial Cleaning, Big Tree Greenhouse & Gifts, landscaping).
eligibility: People with IDD (OPWDD services).
how_to_apply: Call 516-626-1000 or email ahrcinfo@ahrc.org.
notes: Page does not state that businesses employ people with IDD.

name: Job Path
administrator: Job Path, Inc.
description: NYC nonprofit using customized employment to help people with autism and other developmental disabilities find jobs tailored to their skills.
eligibility: People with autism and other developmental disabilities (criteria on its Eligibility page).
how_to_apply: Call 212.944.0564 or email info@jobpathnyc.org; 256 W 38th St, 2nd Fl.
notes: Funding not stated on page.

name: The Arc Westchester Career & Employment Services
administrator: The Arc Westchester
description: Career planning, training and job placement for people with developmental disabilities, including Project SEARCH Autism Enhancement and the Partnership for Inclusive Internships.
eligibility: People with developmental disabilities; first step is applying to ACCES-VR.
how_to_apply: Contact Shari Lewitt, 914-495-4491, slewitt@arcwestchester.org.
notes: Office city not verified.

name: Lifetime Assistance Vocational Services
administrator: Lifetime Assistance, Inc.
description: Rochester agency connecting people with IDD to training and jobs; runs business services including Patent Press and Classified Scanning & Shredding.
eligibility: People with intellectual and developmental disabilities.
how_to_apply: Email info@lifetimeassistance.org; 425 Paul Rd, Rochester, NY 14624.
notes: Share of IDD employees at its businesses not stated.

name: Project SEARCH - Greater Rochester (URMC)
administrator: University of Rochester Medical Center - Strong Center for Developmental Disabilities
description: School-year internship program held entirely at host workplaces (e.g., URMC, Wegmans, City of Rochester) for youth and young adults with IDD: daily employability training, three internships, and job development.
eligibility: Youth and young adults with significant disabilities/IDD (formal criteria not published).
how_to_apply: Contact Marilee Boylan, NYS Project SEARCH State Coordinator, Marilee_Boylan@URMC.Rochester.edu; other NY sites at projectsearch.us/locations.
notes: Funded initially by B. Thomas Golisano Foundation.

name: The Arc New York (32 local chapters)
administrator: The Arc New York
description: Statewide family-led organization for people with IDD with 32 local chapters, many of which run employment services and businesses.
eligibility: People with IDD.
how_to_apply: Use thearcny.org/find-a-chapter or call (518) 439-8311.
notes: State office page does not describe employment services; use for chapter referral.

name: Western NY WIPA Project (Neighborhood Legal Services)
administrator: Neighborhood Legal Services, Inc. (SSA WIPA grant)
description: Free benefits counseling on how work affects SSI/SSDI, Medicaid and other benefits for 22 Western/Central NY counties.
eligibility: SSDI/SSI beneficiaries ages 14-full retirement age in served counties: Allegany, Erie, Cattaraugus, Cayuga, Chautauqua, Chemung, Cortland, Genesee, Livingston, Monroe, Niagara, Onondaga, Ontario, Orleans, Schuyler, Seneca, Steuben, Tompkins, Tioga, Wayne, Wyoming, Yates.
how_to_apply: Call 888-224-3272 (toll-free) or 716-847-0650; 237 Main St, Suite 400, Buffalo.
notes: Source document dated 2025; age eligibility per standard WIPA rules, not on the page.

name: Work Without Limits WIPA (New York)
administrator: Work Without Limits / ForHealth Consulting at UMass Chan Medical School (SSA WIPA grant)
description: Free work-incentives benefits counseling for New York SSI/SSDI beneficiaries via a 2026 NY referral package.
eligibility: SSI/SSDI beneficiaries meeting WIPA priority criteria; others referred to the Ticket to Work Help Line.
how_to_apply: Call 877-937-9675 or email the 2026 NY referral package to WIPAreferral@umassmed.edu.
notes: NY counties served not listed in document (likely areas outside NLS region; unverified).

name: SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, food benefits)
administrator: NYS Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance (OTDA) and local departments of social services
description: SNAP puts money for food on an EBT (Electronic Benefits Transfer) card each month. The card works like a debit card at approved food stores.
eligibility: Based on household size, income and other factors. Households with a disabled member or a member 60+ use a higher gross income limit ($2,660/month for 1 person, as of October 1, 2026). Most households no longer face a savings test. The only way to know if you qualify is to apply.
max_benefit: $306/month for a 1-person household; $562 for 2 (standards effective October 1, 2026). The real benefit may be less.
how_to_apply: Apply at myBenefits.ny.gov or at your local department of social services. OTDA Hotline: 1-800-342-3009.
notes: New SNAP work rules are in effect. OTDA says people who lost SNAP because of these rules can reapply starting October 1, 2026. An autistic adult who lives with family may be counted in the family's SNAP household depending on who buys and prepares food together. Ask the local office.

name: HEAP (Home Energy Assistance Program)
administrator: NYS OTDA, through local HEAP district contacts (local departments of social services)
description: HEAP helps pay to heat (and sometimes cool) your home. Most benefits are paid straight to the fuel or utility company. Homeowners can also get help to repair, replace, or clean their heating equipment.
eligibility: Based on income, household size, heating source, and whether someone in the home is under 6, 60 or older, or permanently disabled. You may qualify by income (for example, gross income of $3,563/month or less for 1 person in 2026-2027) or if you get SNAP, federally funded Temporary Assistance, or Code A SSI (living alone).
max_benefit: Regular benefit (2026-2027): $990 + add-ons for oil, kerosene or propane; $700 + add-ons for wood, coal and similar fuels; $400 + add-ons for electric or gas heat. Add $35 if a household member is permanently disabled, under 6, or 60+. Equipment repair up to $4,000; replacement up to $8,000; Clean and Tune up to $500. Emergency benefits $185 to $990 depending on the emergency.
how_to_apply: Apply at myBenefits.ny.gov or through your HEAP Local District Contact. OTDA Hotline: 1-800-342-3009.
notes: Only one Regular HEAP benefit per program year. Emergency HEAP requires contacting your local district directly; it cannot be done on the website. The Cooling Assistance benefit (air conditioner or fan) for 2025-2026 closed June 5, 2026. Getting HEAP also enrolls you automatically in your utility's Energy Affordability Program discount.
apply_window: Regular HEAP opens November 2, 2026; Emergency HEAP opens January 4, 2027; Heating Equipment Repair/Replacement and Clean and Tune opened October 1, 2026.

name: Energy Affordability Program (EAP) and Enhanced EAP (EEAP), utility bill discounts
administrator: NYS Department of Public Service / Public Service Commission (PSC), delivered by the major electric and gas utilities
description: A monthly discount on your electric and/or natural gas bill. The discount is applied directly to your bill by your utility.
eligibility: Households below state median income (or area median income for Con Edison, National Grid NYC and National Grid Long Island customers). People who get HEAP, SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, Safety Net Assistance, TANF and other listed programs qualify. Since January 13, 2026, some customers below median income who did not meet the old limits can get the Enhanced EAP.
max_benefit: Not published (the page says discount amounts are standardized but does not list them)
how_to_apply: People who get public assistance may be enrolled automatically. If not, contact your utility. If you do not get a qualifying benefit, apply for EEAP online at nyeeap.com (income limits at nyeeap.com/faq).
notes: Covers Central Hudson, Con Edison, National Fuel, National Grid, NYSEG, Orange & Rockland, PSEG Long Island and RG&E customers. Participants are automatically put on budget billing; you can opt out with your utility.

name: Safety Net Assistance (SNA) and Emergency Assistance (Temporary Assistance)
administrator: NYS OTDA and local departments of social services
description: Safety Net Assistance is state cash help for low-income single adults and childless couples who cannot get Family Assistance. Emergency Assistance can help with urgent needs like a utility shut-off, eviction, or no food.
eligibility: Needy single adults, childless couples, and others not eligible for Family Assistance. Eligibility depends on household size, housing, income, resources and other benefits. Adults found able to work must meet work rules. Emergency Assistance to Adults (EAA) is for people who get or are eligible for SSI. You do not need ongoing assistance to get emergency help.
how_to_apply: Apply at myBenefits.ny.gov or your local department of social services. OTDA Hotline: 1-800-342-3009.
notes: Cash SNA is generally limited to 2 years in a lifetime; after that it may be paid in non-cash form (for example, straight to a landlord or utility). For an emergency, contact your local office right away so a same-day decision can be made.

name: CDPAP (Consumer Directed Personal Assistance Program)
administrator: NYS Department of Health (Medicaid); Public Partnership LLC (PPL) is the single Statewide Fiscal Intermediary
description: A Medicaid program that lets a person who needs home care choose, hire and train their own caregiver, called a personal assistant. The assistant can be a friend or family member, with some exceptions.
eligibility: Must be eligible for NYS Medicaid, have a stable medical condition, have an assessed need for home care, be able to self-direct or have a designated representative, and (if 21 or older) meet the Minimum Needs Requirements in effect since September 1, 2025. The assistant cannot be the person's spouse, their designated representative, or the parent of a consumer under 21.
how_to_apply: Questions: StatewideFI@health.ny.gov. All CDPAP consumers must work with PPL (Public Partnership LLC) as their fiscal intermediary.
notes: 2025-2026 changes: the state moved CDPAP to one Statewide Fiscal Intermediary, PPL, which handles payroll for personal assistants. Assistants must also register with PPL to be paid. Since September 1, 2025, new adult applicants (21+) must meet the Minimum Needs Requirements: needing at least limited help with physical maneuvering in more than two Activities of Daily Living (or supervision with more than one, for dementia/Alzheimer's). People already authorized as of September 1, 2025 keep the old rules. For many autistic adults whose needs are mainly supervision or prompting, this new rule may make it harder to qualify. Ask the assessor.

name: OPWDD Family Support Services (FSS), including Family Reimbursement
administrator: NYS Office for People With Developmental Disabilities (OPWDD), through local FSS provider agencies
description: Supports for families caring at home for a relative with a developmental disability. Includes a Family Reimbursement program that can pay families back for some approved costs.
eligibility: Families caring at home for a relative with a developmental disability who is eligible for OPWDD services. Exact rules for reimbursement are in OPWDD's ADM #2022-02R.
how_to_apply: Call the OPWDD Information Line (Front Door): 1-866-946-9733 (NY Relay: 711). Family Reimbursement requests go through your local FSS provider agency.
notes: Services and amounts vary by region and provider agency. Reimbursement guidelines: https://opwdd.ny.gov/regulations-guidance/adm-2022-02-family-support-services-fss-reimbursement-guidelines. The person must first be found eligible for OPWDD services through the Front Door process.

name: OPWDD Self-Direction (self-directed budget)
administrator: NYS OPWDD (Medicaid HCBS Waiver); budgets are paid through a Fiscal Intermediary agency
description: Self-Direction lets an OPWDD-eligible person choose their own services, staff and schedule, using a budget built with their Circle of Support. It can include hiring your own staff and buying approved goods and community classes.
eligibility: Anyone eligible for OPWDD services and enrolled in the Home and Community Based Services (HCBS) Waiver. The person must be able to make their own decisions or have someone to help them.
how_to_apply: Talk to your Care Manager. You can attend a Self-Direction information session at a Developmental Disabilities Regional Office (DDRO). OPWDD Information Line: 1-866-946-9733.
notes: The page does not show an update date, but OPWDD posted new Self-Direction checklists in December 2025. You can switch back to traditional services at any time.

name: NY ABLE Savings Program
administrator: Office of the NYS Comptroller; Ascensus Broker Dealer Services, LLC (Program Manager)
description: A tax-free savings account for a person with a disability. Money can be spent on disability-related costs like housing, transportation and support services without losing Medicaid, and SSI is only affected above $100,000.
eligibility: Disability present before age 46, plus one of: SSI or SSDI because of the disability; legally blind; a condition on SSA's Compassionate Allowances list; or a doctor's written diagnosis of a condition causing marked and severe functional limits expected to last at least a year.
upfront_cost: $25 minimum to open ($15 through payroll deduction). No enrollment fee.
ongoing_cost: $10/quarter maintenance fee with electronic statements ($12.50 with paper); 0.28%-0.35% asset-based fee depending on option; Checking Option $2/month unless waived.
max_benefit: Annual contribution limit $20,000 (working account owners may add more); maximum account balance $520,000
how_to_apply: Enroll online at mynyable.org. Call 1.855.5NY.ABLE (1.855.569.2253) Mon – Fri, 8 a.m. – 8 p.m. ET. NY Relay: 711 or 800-662-1220.
notes: The age of onset rose to 46 starting January 2026, so more people now qualify. If the account owner can't open it, a power of attorney, guardian, parent, sibling, grandparent, or SSA representative payee can. Accounts at or above $100,000 count toward SSI eligibility. Medicaid may seek repayment after the owner's death. Fees from https://www.mynyable.org/home/investments/fees.html; eligibility from https://www.mynyable.org/home/eligibility/requirements.html.

name: NYSARC Trust Services pooled supplemental needs trusts (Community Trusts)
administrator: NYSARC Trust Services (nonprofit)
description: A nonprofit that runs pooled trusts so a person with a disability can keep extra savings or income and still qualify for Medicaid and SSI. Community Trust II lets members use income above Medicaid limits to pay rent, utilities, food and other needs.
eligibility: Community Trust II: people with disabilities and older adults seeking Medicaid home care and other community-based services. Staff can help pick the right trust (Community Trust I for extra savings, II for extra monthly income, III for large settlements or inheritances).
upfront_cost: Minimum deposit of $300. A one-time enrollment fee and the first month's administrative fee are taken from the first deposit (amounts on the fee schedule).
ongoing_cost: Administrative fees per the current fee schedule (amounts not stated on the pages read)
how_to_apply: Customer service: (518) 439-8323. Mail the enrollment package to PO Box 1531, Latham, New York 12110 (mail the check separately to NYSARC, Inc. Community Trust, PO Box 1788, Albany, New York 12201).
notes: Accounts are usually set up in about 5 business days after all papers arrive. Talk with your local Medicaid office or an attorney about how a trust affects benefits. Community Trust II page: https://www.nysarctrustservices.org/nysarc-trusts/pooled-trusts/community-trust-ii/
apply_steps: Pick the right trust with help from NYSARC customer service at (518) 439-8323.
Complete the Joinder Agreement and have it signed and notarized.
Gather copies of the beneficiary's Social Security card and Social Security award letter (plus power of attorney or guardianship papers if someone else signs).
Mail the enrollment package to PO Box 1531, Latham, NY 12110, and mail the deposit (at least $300) separately to the bank address.
Wait about 5 business days for the account to be set up.

name: NYS Child and Dependent Care Credit (Form IT-216)
administrator: NYS Department of Taxation and Finance
description: A state income tax credit for paying someone to care for a qualifying person so you can work. Under the federal rules it follows, an adult dependent who cannot care for themselves can count. Full-year residents can get it as a refund even if they owe no tax.
eligibility: You qualify if you qualified to claim the federal child and dependent care credit, whether or not you actually claimed it. Amount depends on NY adjusted gross income, number of qualifying persons, and care costs.
how_to_apply: File Form IT-216, Claim for Child and Dependent Care Credit, with your NY income tax return.
notes: Fully refundable for full-year residents; partly refundable for part-year residents; not refundable for nonresidents. NYC residents may also qualify for a separate New York City Child and Dependent Care Credit (linked from the page). Page updated November 5, 2025.
apply_window: With your yearly state tax return

name: NYS Real Property Tax Credit (Form IT-214)
administrator: NYS Department of Taxation and Finance
description: A small refundable credit for very low-income renters and homeowners. An autistic adult with low income who pays rent may be able to claim it even if they don't normally file taxes.
eligibility: Full-year NY resident; federal adjusted gross income of $18,000 or less; for renters, average monthly rent of $450 or less; real property owned worth $85,000 or less.
max_benefit: Up to $75 if everyone in the household is under 65; up to $375 if someone is 65 or older
how_to_apply: File Form IT-214, Claim for Real Property Tax Credit. If you don't have to file a NY return, you can file just Form IT-214 to get the refund.
notes: Page updated November 18, 2025. Other conditions on the page may apply (for example, rules for people claimed as dependents).
apply_window: With your yearly state tax return (or Form IT-214 alone)

name: MTA Reduced-Fare Program (people with disabilities)
administrator: Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA) / MTA New York City Transit
description: Half-price rides on subways, local buses and express buses for people with a qualifying disability, using a Reduced-Fare OMNY card. Also saves up to 50% on Long Island Rail Road and Metro-North peak fares.
eligibility: People 65+ or with a qualifying disability. Listed disabilities include cognitive disability, serious mental illness with SSI, getting Medicare for a reason other than age, blindness, deafness, and ambulatory or other physical disability. Disability must be documented (list on page 5 of the disability application).
max_benefit: Reduced fare: $1.50 for subway, local/limited/Select Bus Service and Staten Island Railway; $3.60 for express bus; up to 50% off LIRR/Metro-North peak one-way fares. Fare cap: pay 12 fares in 7 days and the rest of the 7 days are free.
how_to_apply: Apply in person at a Customer Service Center (select subway stations, 3 Stone St in Lower Manhattan, or MTA Mobile Sales vehicles), or by mail to: MTA New York City Transit / Attn: Reduced Fare Program / 130 Livingston St / Brooklyn, NY 11201-9625. Help: call 511.
notes: The online application was not available when checked. Mail applications can take up to three months. Autism is not named on the page; families should apply under cognitive disability with documentation. Covers MTA services in NYC and the LIRR/Metro-North region.

name: Fair Fares NYC
administrator: NYC Department of Social Services / Human Resources Administration (HRA)
description: Half-price subway and eligible bus fares for low-income New York City residents, plus 50% off Access-A-Ride trips.
eligibility: NYC residents ages 18-64 with household income at or below the 2026 guidelines (for example, $23,940/year for 1 person, $32,460 for 2). The subway/bus discount is not for people who already get reduced fare (for example, an MTA Reduced-Fare card) or full carfare from DSS/HRA.
max_benefit: 50% off subway, eligible bus and Access-A-Ride fares
how_to_apply: Apply online at nyc.gov/accessfairfares; upload documents with the ACCESS HRA Mobile App. For help, call 311.
notes: Most useful for an autistic adult who does not qualify for MTA Reduced-Fare but has low income, or for the Access-A-Ride discount (applied automatically once Fair Fares and Access-A-Ride accounts are linked). The Access-A-Ride discount is not for people already getting full carfare from DSS/HRA.

name: Medicaid Buy-In Program for Working People with Disabilities (MBI-WPD)
administrator: NYS Department of Health; applications through Local Departments of Social Services
description: Lets a working person with a disability keep Medicaid even if they earn more than regular Medicaid allows. This matters because Medicaid pays for services like CDPAP and OPWDD supports.
eligibility: NY resident, age 16 or older (coverage up to 65), disability as defined by Social Security, doing any paid work (part-time counts), gross income up to $80,820 for one person ($109,236 for a couple), and countable resources up to $33,038 for one person ($44,796 for two). Retirement accounts are not counted.
ongoing_cost: There may be a modest premium based on income, but premiums are not being charged at this time.
how_to_apply: Submit an application to your Local Department of Social Services office. Medicaid Help line: 1-800-541-2831 or TDD 1-800-662-1220.
notes: If not already found disabled by Social Security, the NYS Disability Review Team does a review. People on SSI who start working may keep Medicaid under federal rule 1619(b) up to $68,654 income in 2026. Work-incentive help line: 1-888-224-3272.

name: EmPower+ (free or reduced-cost home energy upgrades)
administrator: NYSERDA (NYS Energy Research and Development Authority)
description: Free home energy check-ups and free or half-price upgrades like insulation and air sealing for low- and moderate-income households. This can lower monthly energy bills.
eligibility: Income-eligible owners and renters of 1- to 4-family homes (income guidelines vary by county and household size).
upfront_cost: None for low-income households (within caps); moderate-income households pay about 50% of upgrade costs.
max_benefit: Low-income single-family: no-cost upgrades up to $12,000 per project upstate / $14,000 downstate. Moderate-income: 50% of cost up to $6,000 upstate / $7,000 downstate. Extra funding may be available (for example, up to $10,000 for a heat pump).
how_to_apply: Create a profile on the MyEnergy Portal and complete an EmPower+ application, or mail the printable application. Help: 866-NYSERDA.
notes: Some add-on money comes from the federal Home Electrification Appliance Rebate (HEAR) program. Regional Clean Energy Hubs can help with the application.

name: NY State Parks Access Pass
administrator: NYS Office of Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation (NY State Parks)
description: A pass for New York residents with certain disabilities. It gives free vehicle entry to most state parks and DEC day-use areas, free state park pool entry and golf greens fees, and discounted camping.
eligibility: NY residents with a qualifying disability, including a developmental disability with eligibility for OPWDD services. Needs proof of NY residency and a disability document dated within one year (for OPWDD-eligible people, for example a Notice of Eligibility letter, Life Plan, or HCBS waiver document).
how_to_apply: Send the Individual Access Pass Application with documents by email or mail to Access Pass, NY State Parks, Albany, New York 12238. For more information, contact 518-474-2324 during normal business hours.
notes: Processing can take up to a month, so apply early. Not valid at some concessionaire- or partner-run sites. The page shows no update date but is the live official program page. Qualifying for this pass requires OPWDD eligibility for a developmental disability; autism alone without OPWDD eligibility may not qualify.

name: TRAID Program assistive technology device loans
administrator: NYS Justice Center for the Protection of People with Special Needs, through 12 Regional TRAID Centers
description: Regional centers lend assistive technology devices (like communication or daily-living tools) for free, so you can try a device before paying for one. This is an equipment loan, not a money loan.
eligibility: Any New Yorker with a disability.
how_to_apply: Find the Regional TRAID Center for your county on the TRAID Program page (justicecenter.ny.gov/traid-program) and contact that center.
notes: Funded by grants from the federal Administration for Community Living, the NYS Department of Health and ACCES-VR. Loan length and limits vary by center. Call the center before visiting to confirm current services.

name: Autism Alliance of Northeastern NY Individual Grants
administrator: Autism Alliance of Northeastern NY (AANENY)
description: Small grants for caring for, supporting or engaging a person with autism, such as sensory and adaptive equipment, health club memberships, or art classes.
eligibility: Persons with ASD (autism spectrum disorder) in the organization's local Northeastern NY region. Full rules are in the guidelines document on the page.
how_to_apply: Read the guidelines and apply through the online form at aaneny.org/scholarships-grant-applications. Questions: 518-219-0855 or grants@aaneny.org.
notes: Based in Plattsburgh (North Country). The site's region list has no North Country option, so Capital Region is the closest fit. The page does not list counties served; confirm you live in their area. No deadline is listed for individual grants. A separate Financial Planning Grant for parents/guardians is not open right now.
to_check: The page doesn't list the counties served; confirm the service area.
apply_steps: Check with AANENY (518-219-0855 or grants@aaneny.org) that you live in their service area.
Download and read the Individual Grant guidelines on the Grant & Scholarship Applications page.
Fill out the online application form linked on that page.
Explain what the grant will pay for (for example, sensory or adaptive equipment or a class).

name: Federal Credit for Other Dependents
administrator: Internal Revenue Service
description: A federal tax credit for supporting a dependent who is too old for the Child Tax Credit, such as an adult child with a disability.
eligibility: Dependent of any age with an SSN or ITIN. An adult child who is permanently and totally disabled can be claimed at any age.
max_benefit: Up to $500 per dependent (nonrefundable). Phases out above $200,000 of income.
how_to_apply: Claim on Form 1040 with Schedule 8812. Free help: VITA tax sites.
notes: Nonrefundable: it lowers tax owed but is not paid out as a refund.

name: Lifeline Phone and Internet Discount
administrator: FCC; administered by USAC
description: A monthly discount on one phone or internet plan per household.
eligibility: Anyone on SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, federal public housing and other listed programs, or with income at or below 135% of the federal poverty level.
max_benefit: Up to $9.25/month off broadband or bundled service
how_to_apply: Apply through a participating phone company or USAC's National Verifier. Lifeline Support Center (800) 234-9473.
notes: One discount per household. Eligibility is rechecked every year.

name: ACT Today! Family Grants
administrator: Autism Care Today (national nonprofit)
description: National grants for autism treatment, assessments, equipment and safety items, paid directly to approved providers or vendors.
eligibility: Families affected by autism who cannot afford a treatment or service insurance does not cover. Household income is considered.
max_benefit: Up to $5,000, paid directly to pre-approved treatment providers, assessors or materials vendors
how_to_apply: Apply online through the portal linked at act-today.org/apply-for-grant. Fall 2026 round: Sept 15 – Oct 15, 2026. Grants are awarded quarterly; check the site for the next round.
notes: National program. Does not cover transportation, hyperbaric oxygen therapy, or personal needs like rent, utilities or vacations. Decisions can take up to 12 weeks; an SOS Fund handles urgent safety needs faster.
apply_steps: Check it covers what you need: safety equipment (helmets, GPS trackers, sensory equipment, fencing), communication devices, ABA therapy, social skills programs, special-needs summer school or medical help. It does not cover transportation, hyperbaric oxygen therapy, rent, utilities or vacations.
Choose the provider or vendor. ACT Today pays them directly, not the family.
Download the Grant Application Checklist from the apply page and gather what it lists.
Apply through the online portal linked on act-today.org/apply-for-grant before the cycle closes.
Allow up to 12 weeks for a decision. If someone's physical safety is at risk, ask about the faster SOS Fund.
apply_window: Opens 4 times a year. Fall 2026 round: Sept 15 – Oct 15, 2026; check the site for the next round

name: Kodi Lee Gives Back Music Grant
administrator: Doug Flutie Jr. Foundation for Autism
description: Music scholarships for autistic teens and adults: lessons, music therapy, studio time or equipment.
eligibility: Autistic self-advocates 15 or older living in the US. Past recipients cannot reapply.
how_to_apply: Apply on flutiefoundation.org when open.
