notes: 2026 round closed May 21, 2026; reopens April 2027. Foundation is based in Waltham.
apply_steps: Check eligibility: an autistic self-advocate aged 15 or older, living in the US, who hasn't received this grant before. Organizations can't apply.
Decide what to ask for: voice or instrument lessons, workshops, studio recording, music therapy, music business development, marketing or social media help, or performance opportunities.
Put April 2027 on your calendar. The 2026 round closed May 21, 2026.
Apply on the Flutie Foundation's Kodi Lee Gives Back page when it reopens. Awards are up to $1,000.

name: OPWDD Respite Services
administrator: NYS Office for People With Developmental Disabilities (OPWDD)
description: Short-term care for your adult family member so you, the unpaid caregiver, can get a break. It can happen at home, at a respite site, at camp, or during community outings, day or overnight.
eligibility: OPWDD-eligible person enrolled in the HCBS Waiver (or a limited group of non-waiver enrollees) who lives with an unpaid primary caregiver. Not for people living in OPWDD-certified residences or Family Care Homes.
upfront_cost: None. Co-pays and enrollment fees are not allowed.
ongoing_cost: None. Co-pays and cost-sharing are not allowed.
max_benefit: Site-based, recreational, camp and intensive respite: up to 10 hours per day (in-home has no daily cap). Up to 42 overnight stays per 6-month period; camp up to 14 overnights per year.
how_to_apply: Ask your Care Manager (CCO) to add respite to the Life Plan; the DDRO authorizes hours. OPWDD Information Line 866-946-9733; opwdd.ny.gov
notes: Source is OPWDD ADM 2017-01R (updated 3/1/21). Types: in-home, site-based, recreational, camp, intensive (for high behavioral/medical needs). Separate from respite funded through FSS contracts or self-directed budgets. Provider availability and staffing waits vary by region.

name: NYSTART / CSIDD Crisis Services
administrator: OPWDD, with regional CSIDD providers (e.g., YAI, Arc of Chemung-Schuyler)
description: 24/7 crisis prevention and response for people with developmental disabilities and complex behavior needs, and for their families. Includes mobile crisis help, in-home therapeutic support, crisis planning and short planned or emergency stays at a Resource Center.
eligibility: OPWDD-eligible people age 6+ who meet NYSTART/CSIDD criteria. Resource Center stays require HCBS Waiver enrollment, a plan to return home, and age 21+ (18-20 with DDRO approval).
how_to_apply: Family, providers or hospitals can refer. Referral lines: NYC (Bronx, Manhattan, Queens) YAI 212-273-6300; Brooklyn/Staten Island regional contact 718-264-5364; Long Island 516-310-5958; Capital/Hudson Valley 516-858-1540 x1087; Central NY/Southern Tier/North Country 315-362-0800; Western NY/Finger Lakes 844-567-8278.
notes: Phone numbers from opwdd.ny.gov/contact-us (crisis services section). OPWDD notes it is assessing next steps for a provider in Kings and Richmond counties. Cost not stated; Resource Center stays are billed as waiver respite per OPWDD ADM 2017-01R, so marked federally_funded true. In an emergency call 911 or 988.

name: New York Paid Family Leave (family care)
administrator: NYS Workers' Compensation Board; benefits paid by employer's insurance carrier
description: Lets working caregivers take paid, job-protected time off to care for a family member with a serious health condition. In New York this covers a child of any age, including an adult autistic son or daughter with a qualifying condition.
eligibility: Most private-sector employees in NY who meet work-time rules; the family member's serious health condition (inpatient care or continuing treatment by a provider) must be certified by a health care provider.
upfront_cost: None to apply. Employees pay 0.432% of gross wages through payroll in 2026.
ongoing_cost: Payroll deduction up to $411.91 per year in 2026.
max_benefit: Up to 12 weeks per year at 67% of average weekly wage, capped at $1,228.53 per week in 2026.
how_to_apply: Tell your employer (30 days ahead if foreseeable); file Forms PFL-1 and PFL-4 with your employer's carrier within 30 days of starting leave. PFL Helpline (844) 337-6303; paidfamilyleave.ny.gov
notes: 2026 rates from paidfamilyleave.ny.gov/2026. 'Child of any age' confirmed in WCB PFL employee webinar (wcb.ny.gov). Leave can be intermittent in full-day increments. Autism alone may not qualify; the condition must meet the serious health condition definition. Public employers may not be covered unless they opt in.

name: National Family Caregiver Support Program (older relative caregivers)
administrator: NYS Office for the Aging (NYSOFA) through 59 local Offices for the Aging
description: Parents and other relatives age 55 and older who live with and care for an adult (18-59) with a disability can get respite, counseling, support groups, training and help finding services. Some counties let caregivers choose and hire their own respite workers, including other family members.
eligibility: Older relative caregivers age 55+ (including parents) who live with an adult age 18-59 with a disability.
how_to_apply: Contact your county Office for the Aging or NY Connects at 1-800-342-9871. aging.ny.gov
notes: Caregiver-directed respite option per NYSOFA 26-TAM-01 (Feb 10, 2026): voucher value set by each local agency; hired family members must be 18+ and not the primary caregiver. Services and waitlists vary by county.

name: NYSOFA State Respite Program
administrator: NYS Office for the Aging (NYSOFA) and local Offices for the Aging
description: State-funded short-term care or supervision for an adult who needs help, so the unpaid family caregiver can take a break. The caregiver does not have to live with the person.
eligibility: Unpaid family caregivers of adults who need help or supervision because of a mental or physical impairment. Priority goes to care receivers age 60+.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Office for the Aging or NY Connects 1-800-342-9871. aging.ny.gov/respite-program
notes: Priority for older adults means younger autistic adults may wait or be referred elsewhere. Run in 23 counties by six NYSOFA-funded agencies (e.g., Catholic Charities Albany, EAC Nassau, Nascentia Onondaga, Madison County OFA, NY Foundation for Senior Citizens in NYC, RiseWell Suffolk). Funding source not stated; marked federally_funded false.

name: NY Connects
administrator: NYS Office for the Aging with local NY Connects offices
description: A free, neutral helpline that connects families and caregivers to long-term services and supports such as home care, transportation and respite. Staff also help with eligibility steps and applications.
eligibility: Older adults and people with disabilities of all ages, plus their families and caregivers.
how_to_apply: Call 1-800-342-9871 or visit nyconnects.ny.gov
notes: Information and referral, not a funding program. Funding source not stated on page; marked federally_funded false.

name: NYS Caregiving and Respite Coalition Respite Voucher
administrator: NYS Caregiving and Respite Coalition (NYSCRC), c/o Lifespan of Greater Rochester
description: Reimburses family caregivers for respite they arrange and choose. NYSCRC also runs a statewide Respite Registry to find providers, plus caregiver education and coaching.
eligibility: NY resident who is the primary caregiver of a child or adult with a disability or chronic condition (or a kinship caregiver), not already getting respite from another organization; needs a referral from an agency, support group or doctor.
max_benefit: Up to $600 in reimbursement per care recipient; voucher expires 90 days after issue.
how_to_apply: Apply at nyscrc.org; (585) 287-6391; rhyde@lifespan-roch.org or nyscrc@lifespan-roch.org. Find providers at respite.nyscrc.org.
notes: Funded by federal and private funding (NY Lifespan Respite). Eligibility details from NYSCRC flyer posted by CCE Tompkins; the voucher page on nyscrc.org blocked automated checking, so confirm the program is open before referring. Cannot pay for rent/food or respite so the caregiver can work.

name: Article 17-A Guardianship (Surrogate's Court) and free DIY forms
administrator: NYS Unified Court System, Surrogate's Courts
description: Parents or other interested adults can ask the Surrogate's Court to be named guardian of an adult with an intellectual or developmental disability. The courts offer a free online DIY Forms program and help from court staff.
eligibility: Petitioner: a parent or interested person 18+ (or authorized corporation). The adult must have an intellectual or developmental disability and be unable to manage their own affairs, certified by professionals.
upfront_cost: Court filing fee (amount not listed on page; fee waiver may be available). DIY Forms program is free.
how_to_apply: File in the Surrogate's Court of the county where the person lives; use the DIY Forms program at nycourts.gov/courthelp. nycourts.gov/help/guardianship/how-start-article-17-case
notes: Guardianship removes decision rights; consider less restrictive options like Supported Decision-Making first. AHRC NYC's page lists a $20 filing fee when filing without a lawyer. Mental Hygiene Legal Service may represent the adult in some 17-A cases.

name: Supported Decision-Making (SDM) facilitation
administrator: OPWDD; statewide facilitation provider AIM Services, Inc. (Saratoga Springs)
description: A legal alternative to guardianship: your adult family member picks trusted supporters (often family) to help with decisions, and signs a Supported Decision-Making Agreement. A trained facilitator guides the process.
eligibility: Adults 18+ with intellectual or developmental disabilities are presumed able to make an agreement; supporters must be 18+ and chosen by the person.
how_to_apply: Ask your Care Manager for a referral to SDM facilitation, or contact OPWDD (866-946-9733). Background and resources: sdmny.org
notes: SDM agreements recognized under Mental Hygiene Law Article 82 (signed 2022). AIM Services named statewide SDM facilitation provider in March 2026. OPWDD rule says facilitators may charge fees; cost to families not published. Direct AIM contact info not found on checked pages.

name: AHRC NYC Guardianship Services
administrator: AHRC New York City
description: Helps NYC families understand and file for Article 17-A guardianship of an adult family member with a developmental disability. Also helps with future planning (standby guardians) and alternatives like Supported Decision-Making and health care proxies.
eligibility: Person 18+ with an intellectual or developmental disability living in one of the five boroughs.
upfront_cost: No AHRC fee listed; court filing fee $20 if filing without an attorney.
how_to_apply: Guardianship line 212-780-4408; Request Services 212-780-4491; ahrcnyc.org
notes: If no family member can serve, NYSARC, Inc. may act as guardian with approval from AHRC NYC and NYSARC. Fingerprinting and a court appearance may be required.

name: AHRC NYC Family Respite and Family Education
administrator: AHRC New York City
description: Hourly in-home respite gives NYC families a break from caregiving, with overnight emergency respite in Queens and Manhattan for crises like illness or hospitalization. AHRC NYC also runs free family education workshops.
eligibility: OPWDD-eligible person who completed Front Door, living with the caregiver; current Level of Care within the past year unless already in the Waiver.
how_to_apply: Request Services 212-780-4491 (TTY 711); ahrcnyc.org/ric/contact
notes: Hourly respite is waiver-funded (all five boroughs). Page does not state age range or hours. Workshop info from ahrcnyc.org/services/families.

name: AHRC NYC Sibling Services
administrator: AHRC New York City
description: Peer support and professional help for brothers and sisters, children and adults, of people with developmental disabilities. Adult siblings can join phone 'Sibchats' and online learning through SiblingResources.org.
eligibility: Siblings of people with developmental disabilities in the five boroughs, whether or not the person gets AHRC NYC services. Sibshops are for ages 8-13.
how_to_apply: 212-603-9743; sibshops@ahrcnyc.org; general 212-780-2500
notes: No specific adult sibling group listed beyond SiblingResources.org Sibchats.

name: YAI Family Support Services
administrator: YAI
description: In-home and site-based respite so caregivers get time for themselves, plus caregiver education and help managing challenging behaviors.
eligibility: Families caring for a person with intellectual or developmental disabilities (details on YAI Getting Started page).
how_to_apply: Use YAI's Getting Started page or Service Finder at yai.org
notes: Page does not state ages, OPWDD requirement, cost, regions or phone. YAI is headquartered in NYC and publishes Long Island family support guides; confirm local availability. Funding source not stated.

name: Parent to Parent of New York State
administrator: Parent to Parent of New York State
description: Matches you with a trained parent who has been through similar experiences, and helps families find services and make decisions. Also offers online training and the free Text4Caregivers stress-support texts.
eligibility: Parents and family members of a child or adult with a developmental disability, special health care need or chronic illness.
how_to_apply: (518) 381-4350 or 800-305-8817; info@ptopnys.org; ptopnys.org (Request a Parent Match)
notes: Statewide office in Schenectady with regional offices (see Regional Office Contact Info). Free status and adult eligibility confirmed via 211 Lifeline listing; home page does not state age range.

name: Parent Network of Western New York
administrator: Parent Network of WNY
description: One-on-one help, workshops and support groups for families of people with special needs from birth through adulthood. Includes help with OPWDD eligibility and family behavior support.
eligibility: Families of individuals with special needs, any age.
how_to_apply: 716-332-4170; Espanol 716-449-6394; toll-free 866-277-4762; info@parentnetworkwny.org; parentnetworkwny.org
notes: Office at 1021 Broadway, Buffalo; M-F 9-4. Counties served not listed on page.

name: Starbridge Family Supports (Advocacy and GO MONROE)
administrator: Starbridge
description: Advocates help families of a child or adult with developmental disabilities living at home learn their rights and navigate services. GO MONROE helps with transportation costs like bus passes, mileage and ride vouchers.
eligibility: Families in Monroe, Genesee, Livingston, Ontario, Orleans, Wayne and Wyoming counties whose child or adult lives at home. GO MONROE requires OPWDD eligibility and income eligibility; not for families with self-directed budgets.
how_to_apply: Intake 585-224-7359; main 585-546-1700; GO MONROE 585-224-7250, jmay@starbridgeinc.org
notes: Funded through OPWDD (state funding source not specified as federal).

name: WIHD Community Support Network
administrator: Westchester Institute for Human Development
description: Gives Hudson Valley families guidance, training and direct help with disability systems across the lifespan, including benefits, decision-making options and self-direction support brokerage.
eligibility: Families and individuals with disabilities in the Hudson Valley.
notes: Page does not state cost or age range explicitly ('across the lifespan').
